messages.author: cffafe975818feab
messages.subject: Stratified verse unstratified
parts:
Hi all,






I am having trouble understanding how stratified and
unstratified designs given the same data and same transect lengths could
produce very different results. The difference in density estimates is quiet
large, around 15% in each case. My understanding was unstratified sampling given
same data should produce similar results as model averaging should produce a similar
detection function to stratified sampling, where detection function is estimated
for each strata. Maybe I have done something wrong, because I am struggling to explain
why stratified results consistently estimate more animals than unstratified.
Any help appreciated.






Brett




--
Brett Howland
PhD Candidate

messages.subject: Re: Stratified verse unstratified
parts:
Brett, if you have different effort by stratum, then analysing your survey =
as if it was unstratified will give you biased results. If it was designed =
as a stratified survey, it must be analysed as stratified.
